html:
The Chilean coup of 11 September 1973 was the overthrow of President Salvador Allende by the armed forces. Jets bombed La Moneda, the presidential palace in Santiago, and Allende died inside.

Chile had been one of the most stable democracies in Latin America. Under Allende it was deeply divided, and the United States had funded his opponents during the Cold War. The army chief, Augusto Pinochet, joined the plot days before.

The junta closed Congress, banned parties and arrested tens of thousands. Many were held in the National Stadium; the singer Víctor Jara was among those killed. Thousands fled abroad. The coup became a symbol across the world of the Cold War in Latin America, and the start of the free market experiment and the dictatorship that lasted until 1990.
sum: The Chilean coup of 11 September 1973 was the overthrow of President Salvador Allende by the armed forces. Jets bombed La Moneda, the presidential palace in Santiago, and Allende died inside.
